items.q: How does a planet's orbital speed relate to its orbit?
items.correct: v = 2πr ÷ T — the circumference divided by the orbital period.
items.misconception: All planets orbit the Sun at the same speed.
items.why: Orbital speed depends on the orbit's radius and period; planets further out generally move slower and take far longer to orbit.

items.q: What shape is a comet's orbit?
items.correct: Highly elliptical — it speeds up near the Sun and slows far away.
items.misconception: A perfect circle, like the planets.
items.random_wrong: A straight line through the Solar System.
items.why: Comets follow very stretched elliptical orbits, moving fastest at their closest approach to the Sun.

items.q: What observations support the Big Bang?
items.correct: The red-shift of galaxies and the cosmic microwave background radiation.
items.misconception: There is no real evidence; it is just a guess.
items.random_wrong: The discovery of black holes proves it.
items.why: Red-shift shows expansion; the cosmic microwave background is leftover heat from the early hot universe — both strongly support the Big Bang.
